text: Faith is having a good opinion of God. Sarah "judged Him faithful who had promised."
explanation:
"Without faith it is impossible to please Him." But what does faith look like in everyday life? It's thinking the best of God. Sarah received strength to conceive at ninety "because she judged Him faithful who had promised." She didn't have to work up her own faith; she rested on His faithfulness. Abraham "did not consider his own body, already dead… but was strengthened in faith, giving glory to God."

In the New Testament, the word for glory, doxa, carries the idea of a good opinion. To give God glory is to hold the highest view of Him. When you don't understand what's happening, say it anyway: "God is faithful. He's for me, not against me."

text: God said, "Of every tree you may freely eat." The serpent made Him sound stingy, and Eve dropped the word "freely."
explanation:
The first temptation was an attack on God's generosity. "Has God indeed said, 'You shall not eat of every tree of the garden'?" In fact, He'd said the opposite: every tree, freely, except one. Eve's reply shows the poison working: "We may eat the fruit of the trees" ("freely" is gone), and "you shall not… touch it" (added). Take away from His word, add rules to it, and soon you have a bad opinion of God.

The enemy still whispers that God is holding out on you. But He "gives us richly all things to enjoy." He's only against what would destroy you, like a parent shouting to a child near a cliff edge. "At Your right hand are pleasures forevermore."

text: Zechariah asked, "How shall I know this?" Mary asked, "How can this be?" One doubted God's word; the other asked about His method.
explanation:
Gabriel brought good news to two people. Elderly Zechariah answered, "How shall I know this? For I am an old man." In other words: how can I be sure you're telling the truth? He was left unable to speak until John was born, perhaps so his unbelief wouldn't undo the promise. Young Mary asked, "How can this be, since I do not know a man?" She wasn't doubting; she was asking how.

Gabriel answered her: "The Holy Spirit will come upon you… For with God nothing will be impossible." And she said, "Let it be to me according to your word." That's the response God loves. When you hear His promise of healing or provision, don't ask for proof. Say, "Be it unto me."

text: Every morning, look in the mirror and say: "You are highly favoured."
explanation:
Gabriel greeted Mary, "Rejoice, highly favoured one, the Lord is with you; blessed are you among women." The Greek word for highly favoured, charitoo, appears only one other time in the New Testament: "to the praise of the glory of His grace, by which He made us accepted (highly favoured) in the Beloved." It's said of you.

So say it over yourself every morning and before you sleep: "I'm highly favoured. I'm blessed among men, among women." Not above others, but standing out among them. And notice what heaven said next: "Do not be afraid, for you have found favour with God." When bad news comes, remind yourself of that.

text: In Hebrew, "Amen" is the root of the word for believe. And Jesus is called "the Amen."
explanation:
"Abraham believed in the Lord, and He accounted it to him for righteousness." The Hebrew word for believed is from the same root as amen. So when you say amen, you're saying, "I believe it. So be it. It's certain." And in Revelation, Jesus calls Himself "the Amen, the Faithful and True Witness."

Paul said his preaching wasn't "Yes and No," sometimes God heals, sometimes He doesn't. "For all the promises of God in Him are Yes, and in Him Amen, to the glory of God through us." God says yes; you say amen; God gets the glory, and you get the promise. Don't shrug and say, "If it happens, it happens." Say amen.

text: At the sound of Mary's voice, the baby leapt in Elizabeth's womb. Your words can awaken someone's dormant dream.
explanation:
When Mary arrived and greeted her, Elizabeth said, "As soon as the voice of your greeting sounded in my ears, the babe leaped in my womb for joy. Blessed is she who believed, for there will be a fulfilment of those things which were told her from the Lord."

The words you speak carry life. A dream that seems barren, or a promise that feels dormant in someone, can leap with new life when they hear God's word from your mouth. Speak blessing over your spouse, your children, your work. Don't say, "He'll never change." Say, "He'll be saved, in Jesus' name." God spoke light into darkness; you're made in His image.

text: "If God is for us, who can be against us?" The Greek also reads: what can be against us?
explanation:
The little Greek word tis can mean who or what. So it's not only that no person can stand against you; no circumstance can either. The retrenchment, the bad report, the painful breakup: none of them are good in themselves, but "all things work together for good to those who love God." The word is sunergeo, synergy: things combining to produce good.

You can only see one step ahead; God sees the end from the beginning. Perhaps a better job is waiting that you'd never have reached by holding on to this one. Keep a good opinion of Him, and trust Him for the good He's working out.
